cards.method: Wavelet time-frequency analysis (the Morlet CWT: power spectrum, cross-wavelet, wavelet coherence, phase difference — numeric grids)
cards.when: you want to see HOW the spectral power of a macro series changes OVER TIME (non-stationary/evolving cycles) — a CWT power spectrum (period x time) with a ridge & simulation-based significance; or the DYNAMIC relation of TWO series by frequency/time (cross-wavelet power, wavelet coherence in [0,1], the phase difference for lead/lag)
cards.when_not: a stationary series with a fixed spectrum -> classical spectral analysis (the stats spectrum/AR spectrum, #234); a time-invariant band decomposition -> band-pass/HP/Baxter-King filters (#56-61); a plain correlation/lead-lag with no frequency dimension -> ccf (cross-correlation); pure forecasting (this is a time-frequency diagnostic)

alternatives.criterion: ONE series -> a wavelet power spectrum (period x time), the amplitude, the phase, the ridge, the global/average power + surrogate p-values; identifying evolving cycles
TWO aligned series -> the cross-wavelet power, the wavelet coherence in [0,1] (a localized correlation per period/time), the phase difference (an angle -> lead/lag) + p-values

output_key_fields: wv_transform: power (a period-by-time matrix), phase, amplitude, ridge (0/1), power_avg (the global spectrum) + power_pval/power_avg_pval (absent when make_pval=False), period/scale, axis_time/axis_period, coi_time/coi_period (the cone of influence), n_time and n_period

wv_coherency: cross_power (a matrix), coherence (a matrix in [0,1]), angle (the phase-difference matrix), power_x/power_y, ridge_xy/ridge_co (0/1), *_avg + *_pval, period/scale/axes/coi, n_time/n_period
everything is numeric chart-data (charts are the frontend's job ONLY, §5); the raw fit sits in the 'fit' field (to_mcp -> a stub; it contains the complex Wave)
interpretation_traps: the period is EXPRESSED in units of dt; power/coherence INSIDE the cone of influence (coi_time/coi_period) are edge-affected -> interpret only outside the COI
an upper_period above n*dt gives a spectrum lying ENTIRELY inside the cone of influence — no complete cycle — which is plausible but nonsense; the raw routine does NOT error, so a hard gate blocks it
significance = a surrogate simulation (method + n_sim) -> DETERMINISM ONLY with a seed; the CWT power/phase/period themselves are seed-invariant (only the p-values depend on the seed)
coherence lies in [0,1] (a localized squared-correlation analogue); HIGH coherence does NOT mean causality; the angle (the phase difference) gives lead/lag ONLY where the coherence is significant
loess_span detrends BEFORE the transform (0 means no detrending); an incomplete series is silently wrong, so the gate requires a complete one

the white-noise null (the default), against the AR, ARIMA, Fourier-randomisation and shuffle alternatives -> a different strictness of significance; the AR and ARIMA surrogates suit series with autocorrelation
sources: Torrence & Compo 1998 Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 79(1) (a practical guide to wavelet analysis — the Morlet CWT, the cross-wavelet, coherence, phase and surrogate significance)
Torrence & Compo 1998 'A Practical Guide to Wavelet Analysis' BAMS 79(1) 61-78 (the CWT, the cone of influence, Monte Carlo significance)

Aguiar-Conraria & Soares 2014 'The Continuous Wavelet Transform: Moving Beyond Uni- and Bivariate Analysis' Journal of Economic Surveys 28(2) 344-375 (macro time-frequency use, the interpretation of coherence & phase)

cards.method: Spectral / periodogram quick look (a smoothed periodogram, the high-level spectrum pgram|AR, a numeric cumulative periodogram + KS white-noise bands)
cards.when: a frequency-domain quick look at ONE univariate macro series -> which periodicities/cycles (seasonality, the business cycle) dominate; a smoothed periodogram (modified Daniell), a smooth AR spectral estimate, or a numeric cumulative periodogram + Kolmogorov-Smirnov bands for a white-noise test
cards.when_not: multivariate coherency or phase between series (this node handles ONE series); a wavelet or time-varying spectrum (-> #235); spectral causality or connectedness (-> #52); plain ARIMA or seasonal modelling (categories 02/03); it requires at least 4 observations with no gaps

alternatives.criterion: you want the (smoothed) raw periodogram with full control of taper/detrend/demean/pad/fast plus the dominant frequency+period
a high-level quick look, identical to the smoothed periodogram but reached through the spectrum dispatcher (spans, taper)
you want a SMOOTH autoregressive (Yule-Walker) spectral estimate — a cleaner identification of the dominant cycle when the raw periodogram is noisy; the order is automatic (AIC) or supplied
you want a white-noise test (Bartlett's Tp): the cumulative normalized periodogram vs frequency + KS bands; leaving the bands => white noise is rejected

output_key_fields: spec_periodogram: freq + spec (numeric vectors, chart-ready); peak_frequency + peak_period (=1/peak_frequency); df/bandwidth/taper/pad/detrend/demean/n_used/orig_n; smoothed(bool)+spans; method='pgram'; spec_object (the raw 'spec' list -> a to_mcp stub)

spec_spectrum: freq + spec; method ('pgram' or 'ar'); method_label; ar_order (blank on the periodogram route); peak_frequency and peak_period; df/bandwidth/taper/n_used; plus the spectrum object as a stub

spec_cumulative_periodogram: frequency + cumulative (monotone from 0 to 1); band_upper/band_lower (the KS bands clamped to [0,1]); crit (the KS critical value); nyquist; mp; n_exceedances + white_noise_rejected (bool)
interpretation_traps: spans MUST be odd positive integers: the routine SILENTLY accepts even spans and returns the WRONG modified-Daniell smoother -> a hard gate blocks them

the reference cumulative periodogram is PLOT-ONLY — it draws and returns nothing numeric — so it is NOT called; spec_cumulative_periodogram reproduces THE SAME algorithm numerically (centre, taper, |FFT|²/n, zero the first term, then a running sum over the total; the bands have slope 1/xm and an offset of plus or minus the critical value)
the autoregressive spectrum of a trending or persistent series peaks at frequency 0, so the period would be 1/0 -> it is left blank rather than infinite
the periodogram omits frequency 0, so the frequency is always positive and the peak is always a real cycle
detrend=True (the default) removes BOTH the linear trend AND the mean; demean removes only the mean; the taper defaults to 0.1, a split-cosine bell, as documented
the node handles ONE series: multivariate input is blocked, since there is no coherency or phase surface; a gap trips an explicit gate
the FFT + Yule-Walker are DETERMINISTIC (no RNG; identical across two runs) -> no seed is needed
sources: Bloomfield 2000, Fourier Analysis of Time Series: An Introduction, 2nd ed. (the smoothed periodogram, the modified Daniell smoothers, the split-cosine-bell taper)
Percival & Walden 1993, Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications (the periodogram and the Yule-Walker autoregressive spectrum)
Venables & Ripley 2002, Modern Applied Statistics with S, pp. 392-397 (spectral analysis; the cumulative periodogram and Bartlett's white-noise test)
Bloomfield 1976 'Fourier Analysis of Time Series: An Introduction' Wiley (the equivalent bandwidth, tapering)
Brockwell & Davis 1991 'Time Series: Theory and Methods' 2nd ed Springer (periodogram consistency, smoothing)
Priestley 1981 'Spectral Analysis and Time Series' Academic Press (AR spectral estimation)

cards.method: Cross-spectral analysis: coherence, phase and gain
cards.when: how two series co-move frequency by frequency, and whether one leads the other at business-cycle frequencies
cards.when_not: the series are non-stationary and no transformation makes them so; the sample is too short for frequency resolution

alternatives.criterion: you want lead-lag in the time domain
co-movement by frequency band
the relationship changes over time

output_key_fields: phase: phase difference, convertible to a lead in periods
interpretation_traps: THE PHASE SPECTRUM IS ONLY INTERPRETABLE WHERE COHERENCE IS SIGNIFICANT; phase estimates at incoherent frequencies are uniformly distributed noise and reading a lead off them is meaningless
phase is identified modulo 2 pi, so a lead of k periods and one of k plus a full cycle are indistinguishable
smoothing the periodogram trades bias against variance and directly controls how much coherence you see
sources: Priestley 1981, Spectral Analysis and Time Series
Koopmans 1974, The Spectral Analysis of Time Series
spectrum

cards.when: decomposing a series by timescale, where each component can be interpreted as short-, medium- or long-run variation
cards.when_not: the series is short relative to the number of levels; you need frequency resolution rather than scale bands

alternatives.criterion: orthogonal, decimated, requires a dyadic length
shift invariant, any length, the usual choice for economics
you want a fine time-frequency picture

output_key_fields: correlation_by_scale: cross-correlation per scale between two series
boundary_affected: coefficients contaminated by the boundary
interpretation_traps: THE DWT REQUIRES A DYADIC-LENGTH SERIES AND IS NOT SHIFT INVARIANT -- shifting the sample by one observation changes the decomposition, which is why MODWT is preferred for economic data
boundary coefficients are contaminated by the periodic or reflective extension and must be excluded from any statistic
the wavelet filter choice affects the scale bands; a longer filter gives better frequency separation and more boundary contamination
sources: Percival & Walden 2000, Wavelet Methods for Time Series Analysis
Gencay, Selcuk & Whitcher 2002, An Introduction to Wavelets and Other Filtering Methods
PyWavelets

cards.method: Multitaper and Welch spectral estimation with confidence intervals
cards.when: the raw periodogram is inconsistent, and a usable spectrum needs smoothing or tapering with honest uncertainty
cards.when_not: you need the exact periodogram ordinates; the series is too short for any segmentation

alternatives.criterion: simple, widely used
the best bias-variance trade-off, with proper degrees of freedom
you want a smooth spectrum from a fitted model

output_key_fields: conf_int: confidence band, from the chi-squared degrees of freedom
resolution: the frequency resolution actually achieved
interpretation_traps: THE RAW PERIODOGRAM IS NOT CONSISTENT: its variance does not fall as the sample grows, so an unsmoothed spectral plot is noise however long the series
there is a hard trade-off between frequency resolution and variance; more smoothing means a smoother spectrum and blurred peaks
the number of tapers sets the degrees of freedom and therefore the confidence band, and it must be reported
sources: Thomson 1982 (Proceedings of the IEEE 70:1055-1096)
Welch 1967 (IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics 15:70)
Percival & Walden 1993, Spectral Analysis for Physical Applications
spectrum

cards.when: causality can run at business-cycle frequencies and not at high frequencies, which a single time-domain statistic averages away
cards.when_not: the series are non-stationary; the VAR the decomposition rests on is misspecified

alternatives.criterion: one summary statistic
causality by frequency
linear feedback decomposed by frequency

output_key_fields: band_statistics: aggregated over named frequency bands
interpretation_traps: THE FREQUENCY-DOMAIN MEASURE INTEGRATES TO THE TIME-DOMAIN STATISTIC, so a zero overall statistic is consistent with strong causality at some frequencies offset by none at others
the decomposition inherits every misspecification of the underlying VAR, particularly the lag order
critical values vary with frequency and using a single threshold across the spectrum is wrong
sources: Breitung & Candelon 2006 (Journal of Econometrics 132:363)
statsmodels

cards.method: Empirical mode decomposition and the Hilbert-Huang transform
cards.when: decomposing a nonlinear, non-stationary series into oscillatory modes defined by the data rather than by a fixed basis
cards.when_not: the series is stationary and a Fourier or wavelet basis is appropriate and better understood

alternatives.criterion: a fixed basis with known properties
data-driven modes, handles non-stationarity
mode mixing is a problem

output_key_fields: residual: the trend left after extraction
interpretation_traps: MODE MIXING IS THE CENTRAL WEAKNESS: a single mode can contain oscillations of very different scales, which is what the ensemble variants exist to reduce
EMD has no theoretical foundation comparable to wavelets -- it is an algorithm, and its output depends on the stopping criterion and interpolation
the ensemble variants add noise deliberately and therefore need a seed to be reproducible
sources: Huang et al. 1998 (Proceedings of the Royal Society A 454:903-995)
Torres, Colominas, Schlotthauer & Flandrin 2011, CEEMDAN (ICASSP 2011:4144)
EMD-signal

cards.when: a sharper time-frequency picture than a spectrogram, which smears energy across frequencies
cards.when_not: you only need a global spectrum; the series is too short for any time-frequency localisation

alternatives.criterion: the standard, smeared but simple
sharpened and invertible
sharpened but not invertible

output_key_fields: components: reconstructed modes from the ridges
invertible: whether the transform supports reconstruction
interpretation_traps: REASSIGNMENT SHARPENS BUT DESTROYS INVERTIBILITY; synchrosqueezing sharpens and remains invertible, which is the reason to prefer it when components must be reconstructed
sharpening does not create resolution that the data lack -- it redistributes energy, and closely spaced components remain unresolvable
ridge extraction is a curve-tracking problem and its parameters materially affect the extracted components
sources: Daubechies, Lu & Wu 2011 (Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 30:243-261)
Auger & Flandrin 1995 (IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 43:1068)
ssqueezepy

cards.when: the series is irregularly sampled or has gaps, where the ordinary periodogram is not defined
cards.when_not: the sampling is regular, where standard spectral methods are better understood and faster

alternatives.criterion: irregular sampling

alternatives.alt: interpolate then use a standard periodogram
alternatives.criterion: gaps are few and short
you want variance shares rather than a spectrum

output_key_fields: band_shares: variance share by frequency band
interpretation_traps: IRREGULAR SAMPLING CREATES ALIASES AND SPURIOUS PEAKS at frequencies related to the sampling pattern; the window function must be examined before any peak is believed
the false-alarm probability assumes independent frequencies, which they are not, so it understates the chance of a spurious peak
interpolating to a regular grid and using a standard periodogram introduces its own artefacts and is not a neutral alternative
sources: Lomb 1976 (Astrophysics and Space Science 39:447-462)
Scargle 1982 (Astrophysical Journal 263:835)
VanderPlas 2018 (Astrophysical Journal Supplement 236:16)
scipy
